checks.detail: IAM simulate-principal-policy on the lab read role: s3:PutObject and s3:DeleteObject implicitDeny on the lab bucket.
Bucket lifecycle rule expire-stale-cache-artifacts: enabled, 30-day expiry, incomplete multipart abort after 1 day.

Bucket policy DenyObjectAccessOutsideCacheRoles denies every object action outside the cache roles and neither role may delete, so no namespace or epoch can be cleaned up selectively; only whole-bucket expiry. Attributed to the deliberate no-delete integrity design.
All three function log groups searched for a synthetic bearer, a synthetic tag value, an artifact-content marker and both lab bearers: no occurrence.
Same scan; bearer and content values are absent from reader, writer and authorizer logs.
The client-visible apigw-requestid of a PUT and a GET appears in no function log; the stage has no access logs; neither the Lambda RequestId nor the shim reqId reaches the client.

Direct lambda:Invoke of the writer with a PUT event lacking the authorizer signature returned statusCode 403 and created no object. Run as the operator principal: proves the HMAC gate, not invoke permissions of other principals.

AWS drill 2026-10-24: prior incumbent write Y (200); cutover write X to the evolved endpoint (200, readable there); cutback: incumbent GET X 404 (no mixed restore), incumbent GET Y 200 with identical bytes; incumbent write Z 200 and evolved GET Z 404. Endpoints, buckets and epochs stay disjoint; the deployed ZIP (sha256 f865fed9…) and shim integrity are pinned in aws-lab-c1023a.json.
